title: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning: Laws and Synthesis Strategies
data_curation: Agentic data is decomposed into three cardinality axes: tasks D_T (unique specs, deduplicated at sentence-embedding cosine distance >0.15 with gte-Qwen2-1.5B), environments D_E (instances identified by a structural-signature hash over tool/API surface, state schema, transition semantics and verifier; content-only seeds are collapsed, e.g. 2,048 raw math+code generator outputs -> 256 instances), and trajectories D_tau (rollouts per task-environment cell), plus a sparse/dense reward control. Testbeds: math+code TIR (12k ZeroTIR-style synthetic problems), SWE (SWE-Gym, 2.4k issues across 11 repos), WebArena-Lite (5 sites x 200 tasks), AppWorld (250 tasks x 9 apps) + ALFWorld, and a search domain. Synthesis uses AWM/GenEnv for environments, AutoPlay/SCA/RLVE for tasks, and policy rollouts (SWiRL, TDScaling, Self-Play) for trajectories, all re-run in a common harness with a Qwen3-32B generator.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The paper decides how much budget each data axis deserves, not the order in which data is presented, and frames within-axis curricula (GenEnv, self-evolving curricula) as complementary; an easy-to-hard curriculum on the naive allocation adds only 1.2 points at C=32C0 versus the recipe's 8.3. Each run is single-stage RL from Qwen3 base checkpoints for 1,000 GRPO steps with 10% linear LR warmup.
method: Fits an additive per-axis power law L - L_inf = A*D_T^-aT + B*D_E^-aE + C*D_tau^-atau + I, with loss-equivalent L = -log p_success, by profiled weighted least squares (400-point L_inf grid). Each axis is swept over 6-8 nested grid points (32x-128x) holding the others at calibrated values (D_E, D_T, D_tau) = (256, 10,240, 8), matching cells (256,000) and updates (1,000). Synthesis is priced by a discount kappa in L = f(D_r + kappa*D_s) and a collapse ratio r* (synthetic:real ratio where success falls 5% below real-only). Allocation is a Lagrangian/KKT problem under a linear cost model with c_i/kappa_i weighting and a model-size exponent alpha_N = 0.30. Training: verl + VerlTool, GRPO (G=8, lr 1e-6, KL 0.001, clip 0.2, batch 256 prompts; 8K/16K max length) and PPO with an equal-size critic, Qwen3-4B/8B/14B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, 3 seeds each, ~61K H100-hours total.
eval_metrics: Held-out task success converted to L = -log p_success: AIME24/25, MATH500 and AMC23 for math+code; SWE-bench Verified (world-held-out); a 240-task WebArena-Lite held-out split; the AppWorld test/challenge split; Bamboogle plus a multi-hop split for search. Fitted exponents on Qwen3-8B math+code: alpha_E = 0.41, alpha_T = 0.26, alpha_tau = 0.11 (R^2 > 0.97), ordered the same way in all 21 settings. Splitting the environment axis gives alpha_W (world) = 0.44 and alpha_V (structure) = 0.28. Collapse ratios: r*_E about 9.4, r*_T about 3.4, r*_tau about 1.4. Bootstrap 95% CIs over 3 seeds are reported.
key_results: Scaling exponents order environment > task > trajectory in all 21 tested settings (sizes, families, domains, PPO/GRPO), and the compute-optimal recipe D_E ~ C^0.34, D_T ~ C^0.27, D_tau ~ C^0.13, N ~ C^0.26 predicts 51.7% vs a measured 51.3% on a held-out Qwen3-14B run at 32C0, beating Chinchilla-transferred (47.3%) and trajectory-heavy naive allocation (42.9%), a 1.4x-1.7x compute-efficiency gain.
evolution_note: The paper extends Kaplan/Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling and RL-scaling studies (ScaleRL, the Agent RL Scaling Law of ZeroTIR) that treat RL data as a single scalar of rollout tokens or prompts. It reacts to the common open-source practice of scaling trajectory resampling (TDScaling, AgentRL), arguing that this axis has the flattest exponent and the earliest synthesis collapse. It gives environment synthesizers (AWM, GenEnv) and task generators (AutoPlay, SCA, RLVE) a common price scale and turns 'where to synthesize' into a solvable budget-allocation problem.
